span.p: Four places the virtual-memory analogy breaks

div.style: color: rgb(17, 17, 17) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
No fault path.
allocate_slots returns None when the pool runs dry
kv_cache_manager.py:484 and 523. Nothing is demand-paged
and there is no lower tier to fault in from.

div.style: color: rgb(17, 17, 17) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Eviction granularity is the REQUEST, not the page.
The scheduler preempts a whole sequence, frees every block it holds
and resets num_computed_tokens to 0
scheduler.py:566-613 and 1212-1216.

div.style: color: rgb(17, 17, 17) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
The key is a prefix CHAIN, not a content hash.
hash_block_tokens folds in parent_block_hash, so the same 16 tokens
at a different offset are a different key, and identical blocks
are deliberately never de-duplicated - block_pool.py:47-51.

div.style: color: rgb(17, 17, 17) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Discarding is always legal.
KV is recomputable from the token ids, so a wrong eviction costs
one prefill and never costs correctness. No storage tier you have
operated is permitted to make that trade.

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5;

walk block hashes from token 0, break on the FIRST miss,

touch - ref_cnt += 1 and O(1) unlink from the free queue
THIS is what makes a matched block un-evictable

span.p:
Pool sizing on the lab machine
Laguna S 2.1 = 192.0 KiB per token, so 24.0 GiB at 128k ctx
fast tier measured at >= 62 GiB sustaining ~200 GB/s
but any single tensor >= 32 GiB hangs, so the pool must be chunked

span.p:
free_blocks on reversed request blocks - ref_cnt -= 1
freeing is NOT evicting; the hash entry stays live
single_type_kv_cache_manager.py:503, block_pool.py:719

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
get_new_blocks - popleft_n, then _maybe_evict_cached_block
drops the stale hash entry, sets ref_cnt = 1, no zeroing
eviction happens HERE, at reallocation - block_pool.py:647, 679

div.style: color: rgb(17, 17, 17) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Worker side - the same table flattened to a dense int32 matrix
of max_num_reqs by max_num_blocks_per_req, copied to GPU each step,
then walked inside the attention kernel, one load per KV tile.
No MMU, no TLB - worker/block_table.py:81, triton_unified_attention.py:424
